summary: Add active runtime performance profile (profile_id/profile_version/SKU) to standard on-call debug bundle
description:
Requester: Sean Gallagher (SRE)

Context
With the hardware tuning profiles pack rolling out (runtime-1.22), on-call triage has been slowed down by not knowing which profile was active on a given runtime pod/node when a customer reports latency regressions or OOM/fragmentation events.

Request
Please add the following to the standard on-call debug bundle ("debug bundle" collected via our existing internal runbook tooling) for all serving-runtime pods:
- active profile_id
- active profile_version
- detected GPU SKU + driver/CUDA versions (as already surfaced to runtime; if present)
- any explicit override source (fleet default vs customer pin) if available

Acceptance criteria
1) Debug bundle contains a single, easy-to-grep section (or file) with the above fields.
2) Output is safe to share internally and with SRE on-call; should not include customer secrets or prompts.
3) Works for Hosted and Dedicated environments; Private should not break (best-effort).
4) Provide a stable key format so support macros can reference it.

Suggested implementation
- Expose the profile metadata via an existing runtime endpoint (preferred: /health or /debug) and have debug bundle collector pull it.

Why this matters
Recent incidents/tickets required multiple hops (dashboards + runtime logs + fleet metadata) to confirm which profile was in use. A fast, deterministic way to capture active profile in the debug bundle will reduce MTTR and avoid mis-attributing regressions.

Notes
- This ticket is internal-support to track cross-team approvals (SRE + Runtime + Security/Privacy) and to ensure the debug bundle template is updated.

References
- Customer tickets: SUP-21941 (Dedicated H100 p99 regression), SUP-21958 (L40S intermittent OOM)
- Related project: Hardware tuning profiles pack (runtime-1.22)
comments: 2026-01-27 - Sean Gallagher (SRE): We need this before enabling broader canary. During SUP-21941 triage we lost ~45 minutes confirming profile_version and whether the customer had an override pin. Asking that debug bundle include both the active values and the override source (fleet default vs pinned).

2026-01-28 - Omar El-Sayed (Runtime): Ack. We can add profile_version + profile_id to /health (internal-only fields) and then extend the debug bundle collector to fetch it. Confirming with Allison re: metric tags vs debug bundle needs; debug bundle should be minimal + text.

Open question: do we need to include raw knob values (batching limits, kv headroom, kernel variant)? I’d prefer to keep to identifiers only and let on-call correlate to profile reference docs unless SRE wants knob values too.

2026-01-28 - Sean Gallagher (SRE): Identifiers are enough for v1 (profile_id/profile_version + sku). If it’s easy, include a single line with override_source. Knob values can come later; we can always fetch the full runtime config from logs if needed.

2026-01-29 - Caleb Johnson (Observability): +1 to identifiers only. Please avoid adding high-cardinality strings anywhere that might get scraped into metrics. For the debug bundle, text output is fine. For /health, ensure these fields are only in the internal/admin view (if applicable).

2026-01-30 - Ethan Park (Platform): Debug bundle collector can already hit an endpoint on the pod and store it under "runtime/health.json". If runtime exposes profile metadata there, the template update is trivial.

Just flagging: some Dedicated customers have stricter rules about what gets included in support bundles. Keep it to profile identifiers and HW metadata only.

2026-02-03 - Omar El-Sayed (Runtime): Implemented in PR: github/redwood/pr-25014.json ("Integrate profile pack version into /health and debug endpoints for faster on-call triage"). Adds: profile_id, profile_version, detected sku, driver_version, cuda_version. Also includes override_source when pinned via config.

Follow-up PR: github/redwood/pr-25049.json adds a startup log line summarizing active profile; not required for this ticket but helpful for grepping older logs.

2026-02-04 - Sean Gallagher (SRE): Reviewed PR-25014 diff. Looks good. Can we confirm the output field names are stable? Proposing:
- runtime_profile_id
- runtime_profile_version
- runtime_profile_override_source
- runtime_gpu_sku
If that’s too much churn, we can adapt the macro; just want consistency.

2026-02-04 - Omar El-Sayed (Runtime): Kept names as "profile_id", "profile_version", "profile_override_source", "gpu_sku" under a single object in the debug endpoint. For /health we use a flat text block in the response body section "RuntimeProfile" (no prompts/PII). SRE macro can grep for "RuntimeProfile" and parse lines. Adding a short note to the debug bundle runbook once merged.

2026-02-05 - Rafael Mendes (SRE): Confirmed in staging: debug bundle includes section:
RuntimeProfile:
  profile_id=...
  profile_version=...
  profile_override_source=fleet_default|customer_pin
  gpu_sku=...
  cuda=...
  driver=...

This would have saved us time during the last canary p99 regression thread. Approved from SRE.

2026-02-06 - Sean Gallagher (SRE): Marking as resolved once PR-25014 is merged and backported to runtime-1.22 train. Please ensure debug bundle template is updated in the on-call toolchain by end of week. Thanks.
resolution: Implemented runtime profile metadata exposure in /health and debug endpoints and updated debug bundle collection to include the RuntimeProfile section. SRE verified in staging. Rolled into runtime-1.22 release train; safe for internal sharing (no prompts/PII).
